uses.description: signed world scale the body was created with (read-only)
uses.notes: The scale physics built the body's collision shapes with: the parser's signed decomposition of the body's world transform when the body was created (a replicated clone copies its source's). PhysX carries no scale. Composes with position and orientation (same physics frame) into the body's world matrix, including a character controller's: its orientation includes the capsule-axis correction and its scale keeps the controller prim's authored axes. Constant for the body's lifetime. A scale edit (a USD edit or an OVStage transform change) recreates a CPU-scene body, kinematic or dynamic, which stores the new scale; character controllers, DirectGPU bodies and kinematic bodies driven by time-sampled transforms do not apply the edit, so they keep simulating, and reporting, the creation scale until the prim is removed and re-added or the stage is reattached. DirectGPU serves it from a stored device copy, beside the pose. No point-instancer array form.

Constant for the link's lifetime: articulation links do not apply a runtime scale edit, so they keep simulating, and reporting, the creation scale. DirectGPU serves it from a stored device copy, beside the pose. No point-instancer array form.
